reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE is right. Six WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE agreements at $900 for exactly this takeoff are this buyer's price; SheetCount Estimating LLC is the recorded fulfiller with a written quote of $350 per takeoff and stated capacity (two each on days 5, 12, 19), and the plan's delivery performer is SheetCount. Net contribution 6 x ($900 - $350) = $3,300 >= $3,000 after every direct cost. Contractors pay within 7 days of delivery (days 12, 19, 26) and SheetCount is paid net 10 (days 15, 22, 29), each after the matching receipt, so no owner capital is advanced and everything, including the last supplier payment, falls inside 30 days.
findings: Recomputed: revenue 6 x $900 = $5,400; supplier 6 x $350 = $2,100; net $3,300 >= $3,000; minimum cash $1,100 on day 15, never negative; last receipt day 26, last payable day 29 < 30. Ledger matches steps.

Slack is $300 of net and 4 days: one late or unpaid contractor drops net to $2,750 while the $350 payable to SheetCount is still owed (a contingent liability from delivery to payment, not up-front capital).

Payment method is unstated ('pays within 7 days'); if it is a check or ACH, usable cash may lag receipt. The 12-days-to-usable-cash fact covers the first pair, and day 26 + a few days still fits the window but tightly.
Card humanHours is 0.5 per deal; the plan has Brain do every step and shows no owner hours. There is no owner-hours limit, so this does not fail the plan, but the half hour should be stated.
Executor SEND_A_MESSAGE / ISSUE_AN_INVOICE are NOT_CONNECTED; they must be connected (or done by the owner) on day 1 for plans to reach SheetCount in time for day 5.
Exclusion of overflow drywall hanging is correct: no fulfiller is named or quoted.
